Space and Earth Science & Technology
NASA/JPL-Caltech
We are Denmark's largest space research institute and a recognized international institution. With space as the starting point, we develop new technology, conduct research, educate engineers and PhD candidates, and provide advice, innovation and collaboration nationally and internationally.
News from DTU Space
Show all news
20 October 2026
NASA’s Mars rover carrying DTU equipment sets new record in space
NASA’s Mars rover Perseverance has now travelled further than any other vehicle beyond Earth. DTU Space has supplied camera and positioning equipment for the mission, contributing to the exploration of Mars and the search for signs of ancient life.
13 October 2026
GPS jamming over Europe is also disrupting satellites in space
Increased conflict-related GPS interference affecting aircraft and ships over Europe is also reaching satellites in low Earth orbit. An online map developed at DTU, the Technical University of Denmark, makes the disruption visible day by day.
05 October 2026
DTU researchers receive grants from the Villum Foundation
26 researchers from DTU have just received Villum Experiment grants from the Villum Foundation. They are part of a total group of 53 researchers set to test bold, innovative, and daring research ideas.
02 October 2026
Perhaps we can build antennas on the Moon using its surface dust
Over the next two years, Assistant Professor Rasmus Elkjær Jacobsen at DTU will explore whether lunar dust, in the form of a material known as regolith, can be used to 3D print an antenna that could ultimately be manufactured directly on the Moon. The project is supported by a grant of just over DKK 2.4 million from the Villum Foundation.

Astrophysics and Atmospheric Physics
The division conduct research in stars, galaxies, planets, exoplanets, the Solar System and the Universe as a whole, as well as the interaction between space and the Earth's atmosphere.
Geodesy and Earth Observation
The division researches in observation, surveying and mapping of the Earth concerning primarily climate change. Other focus areas are measuring and observing the Earth's gravitational field, displacements in the Earth's crust, ice cover changes, soil and sea surface levels and land uplift.
Geomagnetism and Geospace
The division uses satellites and ground-based measuring stations to explore and map the Earth's magnetic field. The research provides insight into changes in the magnetic field and processes coupled to the sun.
Microwaves and Remote Sensing
The division deals with research, development and use of microwave sensors. We research both passive and active sensors - which are microwaves, radiometers and radars - that are used to observe the earth's surface.
Measurement and Instrumentation Systems
Research and development activities in the division focus on high-precision instrumentation systems for space missions and on research based on data gathered via these instruments.
Electromagnetic systems
The department works with testing, research and development within electromagnetic field theory, antenna technology, meta-materials, microwave technology and terahertz technology.
Centres
Security DTU
Security DTU is a multidisciplinary centre for security and defence research and technology.
ESA BIC Denmark
ESA BIC Denmark is part of ESA's European network of Business Incubation Centres and anchored at DTU/DTU Space. The centers main objective is to create and support space related start-ups in Denmark.
DTU Space Drone Center
DTU Space Drone Center is a local centre anchored at the Division for Geomagnetism and Geospace that coordinate and facilitate research and development of unmanned systems.
